page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.large is a general purpose instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core via simultaneous multithreading. The instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It features 16 MB of L3 cache, hardware acceleration for AES and SHA encryption extensions, and support for AVX, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, does not bundle local storage, and includes no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results show balanced moderate performance for basic single-threaded operations alongside distinct limits under multi-core loads. The instance achieved an average Geekbench single-core score of 1280.0 and handled single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 9.2 GB/sec. However, its Geekbench multi-core score of 1566.0 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 766.59 place it within the lowest 10% tier, constrained by its single-core underlying hardware topology. Memory throughput registers at 23.06 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 15.78 GB/sec for uncached writes, resulting in modest passmark memory and database performance.

Operating as an entry-tier general purpose resource, ecs.g6a.large offers low resource entry overhead without burstable CPU credits. Because local storage is absent, all persistent input and output must travel over network-attached block devices, which interact with the 1 Gbps network baseline. Workloads requiring sustained high parallel compute, intense vector processing, or massive database transactions will encounter hardware bottlenecks. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, low-traffic backend services, microservices, testing environments, and auxiliary operational services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core on a 2.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7H12 processor, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 16 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It contains no bundled local storage or GPUs, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent workloads. Across benchmarks, the server demonstrates middle-tier single-core execution, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1280.0, but sits in the lower percentiles for multi-core compute and data-intensive tasks due to limited core density. The instance serves cost-effective operational roles, making it suitable for lightweight application hosting, microservices, continuous integration tasks, and basic development or testing environments.
